title: SLI contracts and graceful eviction orchestration for model endpoint classes
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Define a set of standardized SLI 'contracts' per model endpoint class (interactive chat, long-form generation, embeddings, reranker) and implement an orchestration policy for graceful eviction and deferred-capacity failover across regions. The outcome is a repeatable SLO declaration format, automated error-budget-based circuit breaker thresholds, and an eviction orchestration flow that prioritizes customer SLAs while preserving overall platform availability.
motivation: Current SLOs are specified ad-hoc per endpoint. We need a machine-readable SLI contract model so routing, rollout, and autoscaler components can make deterministic decisions during capacity pressure and regional outage. This reduces surprise degradations and enables quality-aware shedding (prefer preserving high-quality, low-latency routes).
proposal:
1) Create SLI contract templates for four model classes: chat-low-latency, chat-high-quality, batch-embedding, and reranker.
2) Each contract enumerates: primary SLI (p95 latency or success rate), secondary SLI (quality metric derived from evaluation prompts or accuracy proxy), availability target, and error budget window.
3) Implement a central 'contract-evaluator' service that consumes real-time SLI streams and produces burn-rate signals.
4) Wire burn-rate signals into existing circuit-breaker service to trigger three-tier responses: soft-shed (reduce batch size / lower concurrency), hard-throttle (reject non-critical routes), and cross-region-failover (redirect to standby region or compatible model variant).
5) Eviction orchestration: define eviction priority queues per tenant/route using contract weights (SLA tier, quality-sensitivity, cost priority). The orchestrator executes graceful KV-cache-aware evictions to minimize tail-latency spikes.
success_metrics: All endpoints must have an SLI contract template applied by rollout completion
Mean time to failover < 90s in simulated regional outage tests
Customer-visible error rate reduction during capacity events by 30% vs baseline (measured on Priority-1 routes)
acceptance_criteria: SLO declaration JSON schema published and validated in CI
contract-evaluator integrated with telemetry (Datadog/Prometheus) and outputs burn-rate alerts to PagerDuty
Circuit-breaker thresholds configurable per contract and stored in ConfigStore
Eviction orchestrator able to perform tenant-aware cache eviction without losing active KV chunks (integration test)
Runbook updated with exact failover steps and postmortem checklist
implementation_plan: Week 1: Draft SLI contract schema (schema stored in /docs/sli-contract-schema.md on Confluence) and review with SRE and Product
Week 2: Implement contract-evaluator microservice (staging) and add metrics adapters for generation-latency, quality-eval-pass-rate, and availability
Week 3: Integrate evaluator output with circuit-breaker service and implement three-tier reaction handlers
Week 4: Build eviction orchestrator logic and simulate regional pressure in the chaos harness (region-failover-scenarios)
Week 5: Canary rollout to 20% traffic for Priority-1 tenants, monitor burn-rate and false positive alarms
Week 6: Rollout completion and handoff to SRE with updated runbooks and dashboards
dependencies: ENG-40122 (telemetry: add p95-per-route and quality-proxy metrics)
PM-412 (define SLA tiers and customer priority mapping)
notes: Quality SLI for 'chat-high-quality' defined as 'percentage of eval prompt set passing model acceptance threshold' (daily sliding 7-day window). This SLI is slower to evaluate; we use a proxy (acceptance_rate_estimate) for real-time decisions and a daily check to reconcile. Contract weights will favor quality SLI for customers who purchased 'quality-preservation' add-on.
risks: Proxy quality metrics may diverge from offline evals leading to mis-triggered shedding
Cross-region failover could increase cost significantly if not limited by budget escrows
Eviction orchestration complexity may cause transient increased tail latencies if KV eviction is poorly synchronized
mitigations: Maintain a reconciliation job that adjusts proxy bias and publishes correction factors weekly
Introduce per-customer cross-region budget escrow and hard caps before automatic failover
Add phased eviction (soft -> hard) with KV cache draining hooks to avoid hot-key churn
